card.occupation: Press operator at a metal pressings and fabrication firm in Wednesbury, on rotating days and lates, about 40 hours a week
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive at 16 with a handful of GCSEs, a C in maths and D/E grades elsewhere. Started a college course in motor vehicle maintenance, didn't finish it, and has picked up forklift and abrasive wheels certificates through work since.
card.household: Rents a two-bed terrace with his girlfriend of six years, Kayleigh, who works in a care home, and her eight-year-old daughter, Ruby. They aren't married and have no plans to sort that out any time soon.
card.cultural_background: White British, Black Country born and raised. His dad's side has been in Tipton and Dudley for generations. He was brought up not religious and has never thought much about it. His family are close and practical, and there's a big Sunday dinner at his mum's in Great Bridge most weeks.
card.professional_persona: A steady pair of hands on the shop floor rather than a go-getter. He gets on with everyone, covers shifts when asked and never causes trouble, but he forgets paperwork, needs reminding about PPE checks, and has been late a few times when the alarm 'didn't go off'. He doesn't get rattled when a press jams or the supervisor shouts.
card.sports_persona: A lifelong West Brom fan, like his dad. He goes to a few home games a season and watches the rest at his mate's or the pub. He doesn't play anything now. He did a bit of five-a-side in his early twenties but drifted off it.
card.arts_persona: Not really into arts. He listens to whatever's on the radio in the factory and old Oasis and Arctic Monkeys in the car. He watches the same comedy series over and over, mostly Only Fools and Horses and Peep Show, and puts on the occasional action film with Kayleigh.
card.travel_persona: He's been abroad a handful of times, mostly all-inclusive in Tenerife and Benidorm with Kayleigh's family. He'd rather do a caravan week in Wales or Skegness. He isn't fussed about seeing new places and gets bored on long trips.
card.culinary_persona: Simple and the same most weeks: chippy on a Friday, a bacon bap from the van outside work, and sausage, chips and beans if it's his turn to cook. He'll eat what Kayleigh makes without complaint. He doesn't try new foods much and won't go near anything spicy past a korma.
hobbies_and_interests: Coarse fishing on the canal and at a pool near Himley, usually on his own or with his brother-in-law
Playing FIFA and Call of Duty on the PlayStation late at night
Watching YouTube fishing and car videos
Taking Ruby to the park on his days off
skills: Operating and setting basic power presses
Basic car maintenance and changing brake pads
Calming people down and staying level when things go wrong
card.career_goals: Nothing very planned. He'd take a setter role or a bit more money on the same site if it came up, but he isn't chasing it and hasn't asked. Mostly he wants the job to stay steady and the overtime to keep coming.
card.voice: Quiet, unhurried and friendly, with a soft Black Country accent. He says 'yeah' a lot, sometimes 'ar' for yes, and 'give it me' comes out naturally. He drops in 'sort of' and 'er' while he thinks, and ends things with 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean'. His answers are short, and he echoes the question back ('what do I do on weekends, er... fishing mostly'). Silences don't bother him. He'll leave a gap rather than fill it, and he doesn't rush to apologise. He laughs easily, low and brief, and goes along with whatever the interviewer suggests.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase with few full stops, often just one line. He usually leaves out apostrophes ('dont', 'im'), uses 'n' for 'and' sometimes, and writes 'idk' or 'not rlly'. He doesn't go back to fix typos.
card.with_strangers: Shy at first but clearly good-natured. He's agreeable to a fault, says yes to most things, and avoids disagreeing even when he probably does. He doesn't volunteer much, but he's warm, never defensive, and seems completely unflustered by anything personal or awkward.
small_things: The bacon bap van outside work and how the price has gone up
How West Brom got on at the weekend
Being knackered after a run of lates
Catching a decent carp at the pool last Sunday
Ruby's school sending home yet another letter he forgot to sign
His car needing an MOT he keeps putting off
deeper_things: He sometimes feels he drifted into everything, the job and the house included, without really choosing any of it
He thinks of Ruby as his own and worries a bit about where he stands, since he's not her dad on paper
His dad had a heart scare a couple of years ago, and it made him realise he doesn't know how to talk about stuff like that
He's a bit embarrassed that Kayleigh handles all the bills and forms because he'd forget
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop resting on his knees, angled slightly upward so the ceiling shows at the top of the frame. The light is warm and dim, coming from a lamp off to the left, with the blue glow of a TV on his face from the front. He's a white man with a round, clean-shaven face and a bit of evening stubble, light brown hair cut short at the sides and slightly longer on top, and no glasses. He has a relaxed, neutral half-smile and is looking just below the camera. He's wearing a faded navy West Brom training top. Behind him is a grey fabric settee with a crumpled throw and a child's pink cushion, magnolia wall with a framed school photo of a young girl, and a PlayStation controller balanced on the settee arm.
